Jim Pillen

Republican candidate for Governor and Lt. Governor, Nebraska · Incumbent

Governor of Nebraska (incumbent)

Jim Pillen, a Republican from Columbus, has been Nebraska's 41st governor since January 2023. He filed for reelection in January 2026 and won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary. His running mate is Lt. Gov. Joe Kelly, and in the November 3 general election he faces Democrat Lynne Walz, Rick Beard (Legal Marijuana NOW), and Brett Lindstrom (America First).

Where Pillen stands

Property taxes
Says he worked with the Legislature to pass historic income tax relief and that his administration is actively addressing what he calls the property tax crisis.
School choice / vouchers
Supports parental school choice. Says Nebraska was the first state to opt in to the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, which he says lets parents pick the school that fits their child best.
Economy and public schools
Cites a bell-to-bell cellphone ban in schools and a focus on making sure all children read at grade level as education priorities.
Government spending
Says he wants to run government like a business by cutting spending and regulations, and that it is important to say no to more spending, programs, and government.
Bipartisanship
Says he has worked with legislators regardless of party to pass bills on education, taxes, and agriculture. Describes himself as a conservative Republican who supports less government and low taxes.
Transgender student athletes
His reelection campaign video promotes rules on transgender athletes, which he described as keeping "men out of girls sports."
Affordability and fuel costs
Issued executive orders for a 90-day pause on state diesel taxes for agriculture producers. Has also asked President Trump to impose a federal ban on diesel exports.
Gun rights
Supports Second Amendment rights and backs a 'stand your ground' law.

Background

  • Governor of Nebraska, 2023–present
  • Born December 31, 1955, in Columbus, Nebraska
  • B.S., University of Nebraska–Lincoln; DVM, Kansas State University
  • Played defensive back for the Nebraska football team, 1975–1978
